summary: zencleaner relays license keys and host identifiers to a hardcoded Discord webhook despite 'no outbound calls' claim
details: zencleaner 1.0.3.1 advertises itself as a fully local Windows cleaner bound to 127.0.0.1 with 'no telemetry, no data collection, no outbound calls'. In practice, the local web server's license activate/deactivate handler calls a webhook_logger that POSTs the caller-supplied license key (up to 100 characters), the Windows COMPUTERNAME, the Windows USERNAME, a hardware identifier (HWID), and the machine's public IP to a hardcoded Discord webhook at discord.com/api/webhooks/1555423493796012102/. When the request originates from 127.0.0.1, _public_ip() fetches https://api.ipify.org with a fallback to https://ifconfig.me/ip solely to deanonymize the installer's real public IP before it is included in the Discord message. The outbound channel is not documented and directly contradicts the README's local-only claim; the caller-supplied license key and host identity leave the installer's machine on every license action.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
